lines.text: What if Napoleon had won at Waterloo?
In February 1815, he escaped from Elba with about a thousand men. Three weeks after landing, he was back in Paris, and the army had joined him.

lines.text: On the 18th of June, at Waterloo, 73,000 French soldiers met 68,000 under Wellington. It was close. Then 50,000 Prussians arrived, and it was over.
lines.say: On the eighteenth of June, at Waterloo, seventy-three thousand French soldiers met sixty-eight thousand under Wellington. It was close. Then fifty thousand Prussians arrived, and it was over.
cap: On the 18th of June, at Waterloo,

lines.text: So what if Wellington had lost? Take a guess.
cap: So what if Wellington had lost?

lines.text: Almost nothing changes. Waterloo was one battle on one front. 850,000 allied soldiers were marching on France, from Austria, Russia and beyond. Napoleon had 250,000.
lines.say: Almost nothing changes. Waterloo was one battle on one front. Eight hundred and fifty thousand allied soldiers were marching on France, from Austria, Russia and beyond. Napoleon had two hundred and fifty thousand.

lines.text: Outnumbered more than three to one, he would simply have lost the next one.
cap: Outnumbered more than three to one
